article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis Causes 1.13 Million Deaths in 2025 and Its Decline Stalls
article.articleSummary:
- Tuberculosis caused 1.13 million deaths in 2025 and affected over 10 million people worldwide, per the World Health Organization. Deaths fell from 2024, but 2025 incidence remained about 10.6 million, making TB the leading infectious killer. The decade-long decline (~14%) is far short of the 50% target. Asia bears most new infections, led by India (~25% of cases); other major contributors include Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. In the Americas, Haiti has the highest incidence, followed by Peru and El Salvador. - Tuberculosis remains the world’s deadliest infectious disease. In 2025, about 10.6 million people developed TB and roughly 1.13 million died (≈4% fewer than 2024, −35% since 2015). Europe accounted for about 180,000 new cases (1.7% of global). Thirty countries carry 88% of global TB; India houses about a quarter of patients, Indonesia ~10%, with per-capita burdens over 500 cases per 100,000 in the Philippines, Lesotho, and Papua New Guinea. The Americas marked a fifth consecutive year of rising cases. The End TB Strategy aims to cut new infections by 20% (2020), 50% (2025), and 80% (2030) versus 2015, but funding fell short: international donors 1.1–1.3B/year, while LMICs increased domestic spending to 5.63B in 2025 (+14%). Only ~30% of planned funds were deployed.

article.articleHeadline: Leishmaniasis outbreak? Understand the difference between the cutaneous and visceral forms.
article.articleSummary: Late-2025 records in Corguinho, Mato Grosso do Sul, show 19 positive cases of tegumentary (cutaneous) leishmaniasis; visceral leishmaniasis (kalazar) has not been detected there. Both forms are caused by Leishmania and transmitted by infected female sandflies; transmission is not person-to-person. Tegumentary disease causes skin lesions, sometimes mucosal ulcers; visceral leishmaniasis targets internal organs (spleen, liver, bone marrow) and can be fatal without treatment. Incubation typically 2–3 months (range two weeks to two years). In 2025, MS registered 125 new tegumentary cases with 11 relapses; nationwide 9,984 new cases and 741 relapses (MS: 146 cures, 1 death, 5 abandonments). Visceral leishmaniasis in MS had 38 new cases and 4 relapses with 8 deaths (9.88% fatality); Brazil: 1,331 new, 196 relapses, 125 deaths. Diagnosis combines clinical assessment with parasitological tests; treatment is free via SUS, started sometimes on clinical grounds.

article.articleSummary: Malawi polyomavirus detected in respiratory samples from São Paulo children, marking the first detailed Brazilian and Latin American characterization. Notably, 94.4% of infections occurred in children under three, with low viral loads and often no symptoms. The finding emerged from non-targeted metagenomic sequencing during COVID-19 surveillance, and transmission electron microscopy confirmed virion-like capsids; no viral culture was performed. Malawi polyomavirus was first identified in 2012 in Malawi and belongs to a family with few human-infecting species; historically BK and JC polyomaviruses were dominant. This Brazilian/Latin American report, a collaboration among Butantan, UFRJ, and FMRP-USP, highlights genomics-driven public health surveillance and calls for further study of pathogenic potential and early-childhood transmission; no imported/exported cases reported.

article.articleHeadline: Paulínia confirms the first death from Brazilian spotted fever in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian spotted fever (febre maculosa) in Paulínia, Brazil, marks its first 2026 death: a 45-year-old woman died November 1, with laboratory confirmation and investigation completed on November 11. Lagoa do Santa Terezinha is identified as the probable infection site; Paulínia has two confirmed 2026 cases, with 2025 reporting none. Local health authorities continue environmental and epidemiological surveillance and risk communication. In Amparo, four suspected Brazilian spotted fever deaths in 2026 prompted a Public Health Emergency and the preventive closure of a pesqueiro (fishing site) in Chácara São João due to an epidemiological link with two fatalities. Samples are at Instituto Adolfo Lutz; cases remain suspected pending labs. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, muscle pain, and prostration; tick exposure in forests/parks/riverbanks or at pesqueiros warrants prompt medical care, even before rash may appear. The disease is transmitted by star ticks (carrapato-estrela).

article.articleHeadline: National Health Commission: Priority populations should receive influenza vaccination.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-14, China’s National Health Commission urges influenza vaccination as the most cost-effective preventive measure. Because influenza viruses mutate, annual vaccination is advised to lower the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death. Priority groups should be vaccinated: children aged 6 months and older (if there are no contraindications), especially infants, the elderly, and patients with chronic diseases; staff in schools, childcare facilities, elder care facilities, and medical institutions should also be prioritized. Public service workers with high exposure, such as delivery riders and ride-hailing drivers, are encouraged to get vaccinated. Maintain hand hygiene, cover the nose and mouth when sneezing or coughing, and ensure good indoor ventilation; avoid crowded, poorly ventilated places. If fever or cough appears, rest and seek medical care as needed; do not go to work sick. Influenza can lead to pneumonia; early rest and treatment after diagnosis are advised. In crowded settings like subways, malls, and hospitals, wear a mask according to guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Three influenza strains are simultaneously active in Mainland China; high-risk groups should take precautions.
article.articleSummary: Three influenza strains are circulating simultaneously in Mainland China this autumn-winter season, with influenza A(H3N2) slightly dominant; influenza A(H1N1) circulation is more prominent in neighboring countries. The co-circulation of multiple strains means weaker cross-protection between strains, so infection with one flu subtype does not guarantee protection against others and may lead to sequential infections and a longer flu season. High-risk groups—people aged 65 and older, children under 5, pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, and those with chronic diseases—should strengthen protection and monitor symptoms, seeking timely medical care if illness worsens. In Hubei Province, three strains have been confirmed circulating; most infections are mild, and the overall situation remains controllable with no peak yet. Historically, flu peaks occur from late November to January, sometimes extending to March. Dr Li Tongzeng, chief physician at Beijing You’an Hospital (Capital Medical University), notes these dynamics.

article.articleHeadline: A healthy 60-year-old developed septic shock from Vibrio vulnificus despite reporting no seafood, seawater or injury exposure
article.articleSummary: Vibrio vulnificus septic shock in a previously healthy 60-year-old man from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China (Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine) described for October 2025–September 30, 2026. He denied seafood intake, seawater exposure, or injury, yet rapidly developed massive calf swelling, tense blisters, delirium, tachycardia, and hypotension. Lab markers indicated severe sepsis (procalcitonin >100 ng/mL, CRP 287.8 mg/L; LRINEC 4). Metagenomic next-generation sequencing on day 2 detected 358 reads of V. vulnificus; standard culture grew the organism on day 5. Emergency bedside fasciotomy and debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics (meropenem, linezolid, levofloxacin; later ceftazidime), ventilation, and norepinephrine support were given. By day 9 he was transferred for wound care; six months later he walked normally with no recurrence. The report emphasizes considering Vibrio even without reported water/seafood exposure, noting high mortality in patients with liver disease, diabetes, or immunosuppression and ~80,000 US vibriosis cases annually (peak May–October).

article.articleHeadline: The plague has not yet been eradicated: the bacterium has been here for thousands of years and has no intention of leaving.
article.articleSummary: Yersinia pestis, a gram-negative bacterium, causes bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic plague; bubonic form is the most treatable. Evidence places an early lineage in Latvia over 5,000 years ago, with Bronze Age Britain yielding Y. pestis DNA from teeth belonging to the LNBA lineage that spread across Eurasia (2900–500 BCE). The bacterium acquired the Ymt gene, enabling efficient flea-mediated transmission from rodents to humans; before Ymt, spread across Eurasia may have occurred via domesticated animals. The Justinian plague (541–549 AD) caused an estimated 25–100 million deaths, confirmed by 2025 DNA from Jordan teeth. The Black Death (1346–1353) likely originated in Central Asia, not China. Later lineages diversified; some became less deadly, linked to the Pla gene copy number. Human immune gene variants increased in frequency after plague, with some associations to autoimmune diseases.

article.articleHeadline: A sheep farmer's apparent esophageal tumor was actually a dangerous Brucella-linked aortic leak
article.articleSummary: 66-year-old sheep farmer from Shijiazhuang, China presented with dysphagia for more than 10 days. Endoscopy found a 2×2 cm submucosal bulge; endoscopic ultrasound suggested a larger lesion, with biopsy showing inflammatory cells but no cancer. CT revealed an irregular thoracic aortic wall with contrast leakage, diagnosing a thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysm compressing the esophagus. Brucella serology was strongly positive (agglutination titer 1:800); blood cultures were negative; CRP 114 mg/L. He worked with livestock, often delivering lambs without protection. Treated with doxycycline, rifampin, and levofloxacin, with strict blood-pressure control; plan to place a stent graft after infection control. A second serology on May 20, 2025 showed titer 1:400. He later developed hematemesis from erosion at the aortic-esophageal contact, underwent emergency endoscopy to control bleeding; family declined surgery and he died at home June 13, 2025. Brucella-related vascular infection is rare but carries high rupture risk.

article.articleHeadline: Ginsenoside Rg1 Adjuvant Boosts Immune Protection Against H9N2 Avian
article.articleSummary: H9N2 avian influenza: ginsenoside Rg1 adjuvant enhances vaccine protection in chickens. In a 150-chick trial (three groups of 50 Arbor Acres day-old birds): unadjuvanted inactivated H9N2 vaccine, vaccine plus Rg1, and unvaccinated controls. All birds challenged intranasally with A/Chicken/Jilin/DH109/2012, low pathogenic H9N2. The Rg1-supplemented vaccine elicited significantly higher specific antibodies and hemagglutination inhibition titers than vaccine alone. Post-challenge, Rg1 group showed marked reductions in oropharyngeal and cloacal viral shedding and lower viral loads in respiratory and renal tissues, indicating improved protective efficacy. H9N2 remains widespread in domestic poultry with ongoing antigenic variation and reassortment, contributing internal genes to H5N1 and H7N9 and posing zoonotic risk. Vaccination programs in China, South Korea, and Egypt use oil-adjuvanted vaccines; Rg1 offers a potential safe, natural adjuvant to broaden protection. Endotoxin-free Rg1 (>98% purity) used.

article.articleHeadline: Melting Curve PCR Detects Pulmonary Tuberculosis Resistance but Falters in
article.articleSummary: Real-time PCR with melting curve analysis evaluated rapid drug-resistance screening in 873 TB patients (pulmonary and extrapulmonary) at Chengdu Public Health Clinical Medical Center, July 2024–June 2025, using MGIT 960 phenotypic DST as reference. Pulmonary TB showed high accuracy across drugs—ethambutol 96.23%/96.66%; streptomycin 94.34%/97.44%; isoniazid 88.04%/98.47%; fluoroquinolones 85.71%/94.38%; rifampicin 73.41%/97.49%; with kappa: isoniazid 0.89, streptomycin 0.88, ethambutol 0.78, rifampicin 0.76, fluoroquinolones 0.69. Extrapulmonary TB (102 cases) showed markedly lower sensitivity for ethambutol (16.7%) and streptomycin (50%), while rifampicin (94.74%/92.77%), isoniazid (90.48%/96.30%), and fluoroquinolones (83.33%/93.75%) performed better but with reduced concordance (0.55–0.85). Significant method differences for rifampicin, ethambutol, streptomycin, and fluoroquinolones; isoniazid not. Conclusion: rapid pulmonary resistance screening is reliable; extrapulmonary results require confirmation.

article.articleHeadline: Childhood Infections in Beijing Show Divergent Age and Seasonal Shifts
article.articleSummary: Pertussis shows the most dramatic rebound after relaxation of COVID-19 measures in Haidian District, Beijing, with overall incidence increasing nearly tenfold (IRR 9.93; 95% CI 4.82–20.44). In 2023 there were 104 pertussis cases and 187 in 2024 among children aged 6–14 years, a group with zero cases in the 2015–2019 baseline. Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) overall declined (IRR 0.49; 95% CI 0.35–0.69), though time-trend adjustment attenuates significance; HFMD shifted toward older ages with under-6 incidence falling (IRR 0.37) and 10–14-year-olds rising (272.6 per 100,000). Median age increased from 3.55 to 6.33 years, and the school-age to preschool incidence ratio rose 3.59-fold (95% CI 2.06–6.28). HFMD seasonality also shifted, with the circular mean peak moving from late July to late September (P<0.001). Mumps declined in preschool and school-age groups (IRRs ~0.37–0.39); no major shifts in seasonality. Findings derive from 23,379 Beijing Haidian records (2015–2025), underscoring demographic and timing changes beyond case counts.

article.articleHeadline: Meningococcal meningitis peak season: how to prevent and control it scientifically? Guizhou CDC answers.
article.articleSummary: Meningococcal meningitis (Neisseria meningitidis) remains a risk in Guizhou Province, China, transmitted by respiratory droplets from patients and carriers. The disease peaks in winter–spring, with occasional cases in other seasons; outbreaks occur in crowded settings such as schools. Symptoms include fever, headache, vomiting, altered consciousness, and petechiae; the illness can progress rapidly with high mortality and disability. There are twelve serogroups; A, B, C, W, X and Y account for about 95% of cases. In Guizhou, cases have been mainly serogroups B, Y and C, with carriers of B, Y, C and W135 detected among healthy people. Vaccination is the main preventive method. China provides vaccines for serogroups A, C, Y and W135; immunization-program vaccines are free and target A and C. Broader protection can be obtained with non-immunization-program vaccines (self-pay). Complement with ventilation, hand hygiene, masking in crowded indoor settings.

article.articleHeadline: Phylogenetic analysis of a rare SAT1 foot-and-mouth disease virus incursion in Iran in 2025 reveals genetic association with African lineages and suggests potential transboundary connectivity
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) serotype Southern African Territories 1 (SAT1) caused a rare incursion into Iran in 2025. VP1 sequencing of the Iranian isolate (accession PX608395.1) and maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis place this virus within Southern African Topotype III, with a close sister-group relationship to Botswana reference strains. The Iranian detections coincide with SAT1 Topotype III reports in Lebanon, Azerbaijan and Türkiye in 2025, but spatial mapping shows a disjunction between West Asian detections and established Southern African reservoirs, indicating substantial genomic surveillance gaps that may obscure intermediate circulation. The findings suggest exotic FMDV strains can travel long distances despite geographic separation. Implications include the need for connectivity-informed risk assessment, strengthened cross-border data sharing, expanded diagnostic capacity, and enhanced baseline genomic surveillance to anticipate and contain future transboundary incursions.

article.articleHeadline: Interpretable machine learning identifies patients at risk for persistent influenza A nucleic-acid positivity
article.articleSummary: Influenza A infections in hospitalized adults from Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, show persistent nucleic-acid positivity after a standard antiviral course. In this retrospective study, 432 laboratory-confirmed cases were split into training (n=346) and validation (n=86) cohorts; persistent positivity was defined as a positive respiratory nucleic-acid test within 72 hours after completing therapy and occurred in 29.5% (training) and 29.1% (validation). An interpretable machine-learning approach using elastic-net feature selection and XGBoost yielded the best discrimination (nested CV). Validation ROC-AUC 0.835 (95% CI 0.734–0.914) and PR-AUC 0.714 (0.573–0.851); at a pre-specified threshold, sensitivity 0.800, specificity 0.656, negative predictive value 0.889. SHAP analysis identified C-reactive protein as the dominant predictor, followed by lymphocyte count, age, vomiting, AST, urea, and kidney disease. Potential for early risk stratification and targeted follow-up; external validation and prospective assessment are needed before clinical use. Funded by NMU and Jiangsu Pharmacists Association.

article.articleHeadline: Vaccination Programme Initiation Linked to Lower Haemorrhagic Fever
article.articleSummary: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Jiangxi Province, China, was analyzed from 2005–2024 across 27 counties in the middle Yangtze region. An ecological study linked county-level vaccination initiation to a statistically significant decline in incidence among adults aged 15–59. Across the two-decade period, 7,570 cases were reported. Counties fell into three clusters: I—the heaviest burden (mean crude 7.00/100k; Segi 6.29); II moderate (2.43/100k; 2.03); III lowest (1.25/100k; 1.09). All clusters had winter peaks; Clusters I and II also showed May–June elevations. Adults 60+ consistently had the highest incidence. Period rate ratios declined in 2020–2024 vs 2010–2014. The Callaway-Sant’Anna estimate of the vaccination effect was −1.208 cases/100k (95% CI −1.994 to −0.421), indicating potential benefit of vaccination among 15–59-year-olds.

article.articleHeadline: Are hepatitis B and C co-infections dangerous?
article.articleSummary: Co-infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) means simultaneous infection with both pathogens. Transmission is mainly via blood (shared needles or non-sterile equipment); HBV also via sexual contact and mother-to-child, while HCV is less often sexual but possible. The dual infection often accelerates liver disease; viruses can interact, with reactivation of one driving damage by the other. Co-infected individuals have faster progression to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, and risk of ascites, esophageal variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, or liver failure. Evaluation includes HBV DNA, HCV RNA, liver enzymes, coagulation, and bilirubin; therapy is personalized. DAAs can cure most HCV; HBV treatment depends on DNA level, enzymes, and fibrosis stage. Seek medical assessment early; do not stop HBV meds or self-treat HCV. Limit alcohol, avoid hepatotoxic products, and monitor for liver cancer if cirrhosis risk persists. By Dr. Mai Hoai Sang, Ho Chi Minh City hospital.

article.articleHeadline: What should a pregnant woman do when she contracts influenza?
article.articleSummary: Influenza poses higher complication risks for pregnant women due to gestational changes in immunity, cardiovascular and respiratory systems. In this Ho Chi Minh City report, a 16-week pregnancy with fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue illustrates that influenza requires close monitoring. While infection does not guarantee fetal harm, early medical assessment is crucial. Do not delay care or rely on self-diagnosis. Antiviral medications may be prescribed, ideally within 48 hours of symptom onset, with later consideration if illness worsens. Avoid self-medication with over-the-counter remedies or antibiotics; medications should be guided by a physician, considering gestational age and health. Track fever, hydration, intake, and breathing; seek urgent care for persistent fever, dehydration, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, or altered consciousness. Watch for obstetric signals such as abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, leakage of amniotic fluid, or reduced fetal movement, and consult a specialist.

article.articleHeadline: Imported Malaria Cases in Vietnam Highlight Antimalarial Shortages During
article.articleSummary: Three imported Plasmodium falciparum malaria cases in Vietnam in July highlighted antimalarial shortages. In Hanoi, two patients returning from Angola and Guinea developed falciparum malaria; the hospital had artesunate for only one, prompting an urgent MOH request and a WHO delivery of 150 doses. A separate case in Ho Chi Minh City involved a traveler from Nigeria; stocks had expired, requiring artesunate shipped from Hanoi over 1,700 km. Vietnam targets malaria elimination by 2030, but imported infections persist as domestic transmission declines. As cases become rarer, procurement challenges grow and stockpiles risk expiration, leaving health systems vulnerable. International mechanisms exist (UNICEF with manufacturers; Global Fund; WHO responses). Recommendations: define essential artesunate and oral regimens; locate stocks by referral capacity; maintain buffer stocks and transfer protocols; explore pooled procurement and cross-border sharing; minimize wastage via rotation and longer shelf-life formulations. Emergency donations are stopgaps; durable readiness requires national tracking and international support.

triage.notes: 記事の主題はベトナム国内における輸入マラリア症例への対応と抗マラリア薬（アルテスネート）の供給不足問題。感染源国（アンゴラ、ギニア、ナイジェリア）は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。WHO・UNICEF・Global Fundなど国際機関の支援は既に行われているが、排除期における薬剤調達体制の構造的脆弱性が指摘されており、今後の制度改善・続報を注視すべき内容。

article.articleHeadline: River Confluence Microbes Show Complex Genomic Potential During Mass
article.articleSummary: At the Sangam confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna in Prayagraj, India, the Mahakumbh pilgrimage triggers episodic perturbations of river microbiota, with major inputs of organic matter, nutrients, pharmaceuticals, personal-care products, fecal material, and skin microbes from upstream runoff. 16S rRNA sequencing shows baseline dominance of Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, and Bacteroidetes, including Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Bacillus, Aeromonas, and Streptomyces; during mass bathing, blooms of Escherichia, Klebsiella, and Vibrio appear, with metal-tolerant taxa rising. Pre-event BOD is 2.37 mg/L, rising to ~6.37 mg/L during the festival and about 4.93 mg/L post-event; earlier festivals reported BOD 14 mg/L, COD 67 mg/L, ammonium 2.15 mg/L, and a ~130-fold biomass increase with 792 and 482 MPN/100 mL for total and fecal coliforms. COD peaks near 30 mg/L; pH shifts from 8.17 to 8.53, then 8.33; DO declines with respiration. The review defines genomic resilience as a population’s capacity to maintain or recover function after disturbance via genetic or regulatory changes, and distinguishes it from resistance, acclimation, and adaptation. An observational ecogenomic framework is proposed, noting many taxa are freshwater natives and source attribution remains unresolved.

article.articleHeadline: Goats may contract Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) in cold weather; learn the symptoms and preventive measures.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-14, in Gonda district, Uttar Pradesh, India, goats face a winter risk from Peste des petits ruminants (PPR), a contagious viral disease primarily affecting goats and sheep. Transmission occurs through direct contact and exposure to nasal and oral secretions from an infected animal. Affected animals may develop high fever, ocular and nasal discharge, oral ulcers, diarrhea, and sometimes respiratory distress; mortality can be high if not treated promptly. Deputy Chief Veterinary Officer Dr. Rakesh Kumar Tiwari of Government Veterinary Hospital, Gonda, urges prompt isolation and veterinary consultation for suspected cases. Vaccination is the primary preventive measure; the district aims to vaccinate three lakh goats this season. Additional measures include parasite control under veterinary guidance, clean housing, good nutrition, and proper ventilation; do not administer medicines without professional advice.

article.articleHeadline: 241 rabid stray dogs identified in Chennai this year
article.articleSummary: 241 rabies cases identified in Chennai among stray dogs since January 2026, with 68 deaths following ABC (animal birth control) surgeries; postmortem tests confirmed rabies. Activists warn the numbers are alarming, highlighting asymptomatic (dumb) rabies that public health surveillance may miss. The data prompt questions about mass vaccination drives, which GCC has funded at about Rs 3 crore annually for the past two years. By comparison, Madras Veterinary College recorded 428 confirmed canine rabies cases from 2010–2019 (about 48/year), making 241 in 10 months a notable rise. A dedicated rabies control team began in January; there is no official prior-year data. Population estimates: 2025 ~180,000 strays with 80% vaccinated; 2026 ~200,000 with 87% covered Aug–Nov at Rs 3.5 crore. Ring vaccination within 2.5 km and sanitisation of ABC centres; no reliable live test exists and rabies is confirmed only postmortem.

article.articleHeadline: First HIV-2 case detected in Kushinagar; infection found in a person who had returned from Bengaluru.
article.articleSummary: A 65-year-old man from Tamkuhi Raj tehsil village in Kushinagar district, who had returned from Bengaluru, has been confirmed as the first HIV-2 infection in Kushinagar. Initial ICTC testing on October 12 was positive; a confirmatory sample was sent to BRD Medical College, Gorakhpur, and on November 12 HIV-2 was confirmed. The patient has begun treatment and counseling to identify exposure and contacts. HIV-2 is generally slower and less common than HIV-1, but spreads via the same routes: unprotected sex, infected blood or needles, unsafe medical equipment, and mother-to-child transmission (lower risk for HIV-2). All essential antiretroviral medicines are available at Kushinagar Medical College, per Dr. KP Gond, Principal.

article.articleHeadline: Raichur: 21,926 TB cases detected in the district over five years.
article.articleSummary: Raichur district, Karnataka, logged 21,926 tuberculosis (TB) cases over five years (2022–2026), with 1,106 TB deaths in that period. TB testing against targets varied: 2022 target 54,775 tests with 46,841 performed (86%); 4,896 target cases and 4,815 detected (252 deaths). 2023 target 68,797 tests with 51,657 (76%); 5,853 target cases and 5,085 detected (232 deaths). 2024 target 67,355 tests; 98% achieved; 5,256 target cases and 4,662 detected (230 deaths). 2025 target 68,797; 71,006 tests (103%); 4,656 target cases and 4,251 detected (260 deaths)—the highest annual TB deaths in the period. 2026 target 49,726; 49,203 tests (99%); 3,880 target cases and 3,113 detected (132 deaths). Early detection and reducing mortality remain challenges; symptoms warranting testing include cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss for over two weeks. Six months of free TB treatment; door-to-door active case finding continues.

article.articleHeadline: Host Protein TRIM62 Promotes Influenza A Entry by Regulating Endosomal
article.articleSummary: Influenza A virus entry is promoted by host TRIM62 in human lung-derived A549 cells (IISER Mohali, India). TRIM62 depletion reduces infection by 73% and nuclear import of viral ribonucleoproteins by 61%; plaque assays show ~50-fold fewer infectious virions. TRIM62 drives endocytic uptake, not surface binding; endocytosis declined ~43–46% at 30 minutes post-infection. Bypassing endocytosis via acidified fusion at the plasma membrane largely restores M1 uncoating but leaves gene expression attenuated, indicating additional post-entry roles. The uptake depends on cholesterol-sensitive, lipid raft–mediated endocytosis; cholera toxin B uptake fell 39%, cholesterol depletion inhibited entry. TRIM62 colocalizes with WASH1 and FAM21 at lamellipodia, implicating the pentameric WASH complex: depletion of WASH1, CCDC53, SWIP, Strumpellin markedly reduces nucleoprotein expression; FAM21 or VPS35 depletion enhances it, underscoring opposing regulatory roles. Re-expression of TRIM62 rescues infection.

article.articleHeadline: PCMC Reports 99 Dengue Cases, Platelet Shortage In Pimpri-Chinchwad
article.articleSummary: Pimpri-Chinchwad (PCMC) reports 99 dengue cases and 15 malaria cases to date, with fever cases rising across the city, straining blood supplies. Dengue-driven demand has left platelets in short supply; single-donor platelets (SDP) are particularly scarce. YCM Hospital blood centre issued 38 random-donor platelet bags in a single day, with limited stocks across A, B, AB, and O, and negatives especially tight. Platelets have a five-day shelf life, making large reserves impractical; when required, single donors are mobilized. Plasma and regular blood units remain adequate. Authorities warn the outbreak could extend to private hospitals. Blood banks urge voluntary donations and blood drives during the festive season. PCMC notes guppy fish breeding centers for mosquito control at ward offices, though residents allege insufficient distribution; fogging and public awareness are being intensified to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Breeding sites of dengue-carrying mosquitoes found inside homes in Bhopal: larvae found in 4,208 houses, fines to be imposed.

A joint health department and municipal corporation survey of 89,702 households found mosquito larvae in 4,208 homes and in 5,023 water containers; on-the-spot destruction of larvae was carried out. In total, 638,591 containers were inspected. Dengue cases total 206 and malaria 13 this year; dengue rose from 156 by Oct 27 to 206 by Nov 14, with 50 new cases in this period. Spot fines will be imposed for lapses. Control measures include fogging and releasing 105,000 Gambusia fish into permanent and temporary water bodies to feed on larvae. Since September, home surveys target coolers, tanks, pots; containers should be covered and water changed regularly. April data: 44 teams surveyed 138,774 homes; 3,246 containers had larvae removed; sentinel centers at AIIMS, Gandhi Medical College, BMHRC, JP Hospital, and Civil Hospital Bairagarh.

article.articleHeadline: Keiner Granados: The Ordeal of the Young Man Who Developed Lymphatic Filariasis After a Bite and Appeals for Help With His Treatment
article.articleSummary: Keiner José Granados Sarmiento, 17, from Barrancabermeja, Santander, Colombia, developed lymphatic filariasis after a mosquito bite at age 10, resulting in progressive swelling of the right lower limb, reduced mobility, and reliance on virtual schooling. Diagnosed in 2023, the infection damages lymphatic vessels and can cause limb lymphedema. Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) was not furnished by EPS Sanitas, with the family noting drug shortages in Colombia; his mother obtained the medication in India with a medical prescription and paid import taxes, administering it without a follow-up confirmatory test. A Mexico City treatment plan for 3–4 months, including hospitalization and care, is proposed, costing about 90 million COP. A fundraising telethon is planned for 27 November 2026 in Barrancabermeja to raise funds, while the family appeals to local and national authorities and the president for medical support. The World Health Organization defines lymphatic filariasis as a neglected tropical disease caused by parasites transmitted by mosquito bites, potentially causing limb swelling.

article.articleHeadline: India Study Identifies Essential Functions for Tuberculosis Private Sector
article.articleSummary: India's tuberculosis private-sector engagement, analyzed in a mixed-methods study covering 2017–2024, finds that sustaining care delivery hinges on hub-and-spoke delivery and dedicated field cadres during a shift from donor-supported to domestically financed programs. In eight states, the Joint Effort for Elimination of Tuberculosis substantially boosted private-sector TB notifications and improved diagnostic and treatment metrics, illustrating the value of structured public-private mix. However, the transition to domestic financing introduced operational variability: fewer dedicated human resources, procurement and disbursement delays, adoption of output-based reimbursement, and uneven patient-support functions. Despite strains, local government staff preserved program continuity. Key learnings identify active notification, sample transport, adherence and ADR counseling, and stable commodity supplies as core mandatory functions to safeguard in any public-private mix under domestic funding. The findings stress safeguarding essential frontline functions as donor financing declines.

article.articleHeadline: A Deadly Virus Is Taking More and More Lives: Thousands Infected and New Victims.
article.articleSummary: Measles in the United States has reached 5,412 cases across 45 states, with 10 deaths this year (7 in Pennsylvania, 2 in Wisconsin, 1 in New York). Preschool vaccination coverage fell to 92% from 95% in 2019; herd immunity requires at least 95%. About 300,000 children starting preschool this year remain unvaccinated. Measles is highly contagious: one case can infect up to 90% of nearby unvaccinated individuals, and the virus can linger in air or on surfaces for up to two hours. Complications include ear infections or diarrhea in ~10%, hospitalization in ~20%, pneumonia in ~5%, encephalitis ~0.1%, and death ~0.1% from respiratory or neurological complications. Two-dose MMR vaccination (12–15 months and 4–6 years) provides ~97% protection. Europe reports an imported Ebola case in a British healthcare worker from Congo; patient is in stable condition.

article.articleHeadline: Quarantine for Ebola? U.S. Embassy Announces Drastic Measure for Peruvian Travelers: Here's the New Mandatory Requirement.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo prompts new U.S. travel safeguards. Since November 3, 2026, the CDC requires passengers bound for the United States—including those with layovers—to complete a mandatory health declaration before boarding, available in physical or digital form at check-in or prior to boarding. The declaration requires travelers to confirm they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the preceding 21 days. Those who were in Congo within that window face boarding restrictions, and individuals who do not present the declaration will be denied boarding, with limited exceptions. The measure applies to all passengers on international flights to the United States, including those making connections; airlines are responsible for requesting the declaration. As of November 12, the CDC reports no confirmed U.S. cases linked to this outbreak, and the overall risk to the U.S. population remains low.

triage.headline_ja: エボラによる検疫？米国大使館がペルー人渡航者に厳格な新措置を発表：義務的な新要件とは
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行を受け、米国CDCが渡航制限・健康申告を義務化しており、IHR基準の複数（重篤性・異常性・国際的拡大・渡航制限）に該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事はペルー人渡航者向けの米国渡航規制に焦点を当てているが、根本原因はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）のエボラ流行であるため、DRCのみを発生国として検証。米国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: A deadly epidemic is killing hippopotamuses. Dozens of corpses.
article.articleSummary: Anthrax is killing hippos in Virunga National Park, Democratic Republic of Congo, with 28 deaths over about four weeks; carcasses were found along the Semuliki River. Laboratory analyses by Virunga Doctors and the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN) confirmed Bacillus anthracis as the cause. Anthrax spores can persist in soil for decades, enabling transmission from contaminated soil, vegetation, or water; human infection can occur via contact with infected or dead animals or by eating contaminated meat. The outbreak follows a 2025 episode that killed 65 hippos in the same ecosystem; by February 2026 the hippo population remained over 2,700 in 171 groups. Authorities monitor and remove carcasses; residents are advised not to touch or eat suspected bodies. The crisis is compounded by regional conflict and Ebola concerns, prompting a One Health protection approach.

triage.headline_ja: 致命的な感染症がカバを殺している。数十体の死骸。
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国ヴィルンガ国立公園でカバの炭疽菌感染による大量死（28頭）が発生しているが、現時点で人への感染確認はなく、2025年にも同様の事例があり繰り返し発生している事象であるため、フルRRAには至らないが動物由来感染症としての継続監視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は主にカバ（動物）の炭疽菌感染による大量死を報じており、人への感染例は報告されていない。ただし炭疽菌胞子は土壌中で数十年残存し、死骸や汚染された肉との接触によるヒトへの感染リスクが指摘されている。また地域紛争とエボラ熱への懸念も言及されているが、エボラの実際の発生状況については詳細不明。One Healthアプローチでの対応が進められている点から、状況の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: National Assembly: Singoma Mwanza calls on the Government to intensify efforts despite the decline in Ebola infections.
article.articleSummary: National Assembly member Singoma Mwanza urged the government to intensify the Ebola virus disease response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, even as infections decline. After November 13 hearings with Public Health Minister Roger Kamba, Mwanza noted the August peak reached about 120 daily cases, but deaths continue in affected communities, signaling the outbreak is not yet controlled. He called for maintaining and strengthening response efforts until the epidemic is halted. The session also examined the free maternity policy announced by President Tshisekedi on June 30, 2022, amid financing challenges. Kamba presented new mechanisms—such as a health promotion tax (TPS) and health insurance—but Mwanza stressed that funds must actually reach health facilities delivering care to pregnant women and newborns. The commission will continue oversight of financing, equipment, and care, and Mwanza praised Tshisekedi’s peace efforts in the East.

triage.headline_ja: 国民議会：シンゴマ・ムワンザ議員、エボラ感染減少にもかかわらず政府に対応強化を要請
triage.triage_reason: DRCで continuing Ebola outbreakにより死者が発生し続けており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）とWPRO基準（重症度・持続曝露・流行性・管理可能性）を複数満たすため、社会的・政治的関心も高くフルRRA対象と判断。
triage.notes: 8月のピーク時には1日約120例の感染が報告され、現在は減少傾向にあるが死亡例が継続しており、アウトブレイクは未収束との議会発言。既知の進行中アウトブレイクに関する政治的フォローアップ記事。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in the DRC: Coffins for Dignified Burials.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak declared May 15, 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the 17th Ebola epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo strain and centered in Ituri with early cases traced March–April 2026. In eastern DRC the outbreak persists, shaping both tragedy and livelihoods. Baraka Mumbere, a coffin maker in Beni, reports selling up to four coffins daily to families preparing burials, sustaining his family and enabling a new employee. Coffins range from $100 to $2,000, with orders carried to burial sites by motorcycle. Mumbere emphasizes he does not welcome deaths but must meet demand and support families through mourning, while taking precautions to prevent contamination. He hopes the epidemic is defeated to spare families and end his reliance on Ebola-related fatalities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：尊厳ある埋葬のための棺
triage.triage_reason: DRCで第17次エボラ流行が継続中であり、死亡例が報告されていることから公衆衛生上深刻かつ異常な事象としてIHR基準に2つ該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ流行による棺製造業者の生活への影響を取り上げた経済・社会面の記事であり、疫学的詳細（感染者数、致死率、対応状況など）は限定的。続報で感染状況の詳細確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: CDC Travel Health Notices: Key Outbreak Alerts for Clinicians
article.articleSummary: As of 14 November 2026, CDC Travel Health Notices flag escalating Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) with Level 4 travel bans for Ituri and North Kivu; Level 3 for Haut-Uélé and Tshopo; Level 2 precautions across DRC and Uganda; Level 1 in Kenya. Bundibugyo Ebola has no licensed vaccine and incubation can reach 21 days, so asymptomatic travelers may pass entry screening; clinicians should obtain 21‑day travel histories from febrile patients and isolate suspected cases using strict viral hemorrhagic fever PPE. Other alerts include Level 2 yellow fever in Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana (vaccination at least 10 days before departure); Level 2 global polio notice; Level 1 hepatitis A in Costa Rica; Level 2 chikungunya in Nicaragua; Level 1 dengue. Clinicians should perform 4–6 week pre-travel evaluations, align immunizations and malaria prophylaxis, and integrate notices into EHR triage for patient protection and facility preparedness.

triage.headline_ja: CDC渡航健康情報：臨床医のための主要アウトブレイク警報
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス病の拡大に伴いCDCがLevel4渡航禁止を発出しており、IHR4基準すべてに該当する深刻な公衆衛生事象である。
triage.notes: 記事はCDC渡航健康情報のまとめであり、DRCのブンディブギョ・エボラ（Level4/3/2）が主題。ガーナ・ブルキナファソ・コートジボワールでの黄熱病Level2、ニカラグアのチクングニア熱、コスタリカのA型肝炎なども言及されるが対象国リストにはガーナのみ該当。DRC以外の国は渡航情報の一部として併記されているのみで主題ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: In the DRC's main epicenter, first treatment trials rekindle hope
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo's Bunia, the outbreak's main epicenter, sees the launch of first treatment trials testing several vaccines and therapies. The aim is to protect people from infection and improve survival among those who fall ill. Field operations include a white tent where investigators coordinate trial activities amid ongoing transmission. As the first treatment trials unfold, the efforts rekindle hope that vaccines and therapies can alter the outbreak's trajectory in a region repeatedly hit by Ebola. The piece underscores the ongoing risk of Ebola in the DRC and the push for vaccines and therapies to reduce transmission and mortality.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国の主要流行地で初の治療薬試験が開始、希望が再燃
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行地で感染拡大が継続中であり、重篤な公衆衛生影響と国際的拡大リスクの両方が認められるためIHR基準を2つ満たす。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC東部ブニア（主要流行地）での治療薬・ワクチン試験開始を報じており、感染伝播が継続中であることを示唆。既存の流行継続中の事案と考えられるため、過去の評価状況との整合性確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: PJ.2.1 COVID-19 Variant Spreading, Already Detected in Singapore, What Is the Situation in Indonesia?
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 PJ.2.1, a subvariant of Omicron in the JN.1 lineage, has drawn attention after spreading to regions including Singapore. As of November 13, 2026, Indonesia reports no detection of PJ.2.1 and maintains genomic surveillance using Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) to confirm any suspected samples. First identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026, PJ.2.1 has since been reported in the United States, Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore. While spike protein mutations warrant monitoring, there is currently no clinical evidence that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease, higher hospitalization risk, or increased mortality compared with previous Omicron variants. Public health guidance emphasizes hand hygiene, cough etiquette, masking when ill or in risk settings, and prompt medical consultation for worsening symptoms. The Ministry of Health advises maintaining vigilance without panic, with extra care for the elderly and those with comorbidities.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19変異株PJ.2.1が拡大、シンガポールでも検出 ― インドネシアの状況は？
triage.triage_reason: 新規Omicron系統PJ.2.1がカナダ発で複数国に拡大しているが、重症度増加の臨床的根拡はなく、インドネシアでは未検出・監視継続中のため、現時点ではフルRRAに進めるほどの深刻性は確認できない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア国内における新変異株PJ.2.1の未検出状況と監視体制について報じているが、インドネシアでの実際の発生は確認されていないため、verified_locationsは空とした。発生国はカナダ（初検出）、米国、欧州、豪州、NZ、シンガポールだが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: High malaria cases: Three regencies in West Papua under the spotlight.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, remains high in West Papua, Indonesia. In West Papua Province, three regencies show elevated malaria: Manokwari Regency with 3,702 cases (API 11.14 per 1,000), Teluk Wondama with 2,063 cases (API 29.97), and Manokwari Selatan with 1,204 cases (API 21.3). Across January–August 2026, West Papua reports 8,234 malaria positives, with three of seven regencies in the high endemicity category. Medium endemicity exists in Teluk Bintuni (632; API 3.86), Kaimana (366; API 4.14), and Fakfak (248; API 1.44). Pegunungan Arfak is reported as malaria-eliminated, while border areas near South Papua Province require targeted interventions. Authorities discussed 2027 control strategies with Papua Barat Daya to address cross-border transmission, notably between Teluk Bintuni (West Papua) and Sorong Selatan (South Papua). Nationwide malaria in 2025 reached 706,297 cases, concentrated in Tanah Papua provinces (~674,046).

triage.headline_ja: マラリア感染者数が高水準:西パプアの3県が注目される
triage.triage_reason: 西パプアにおけるマラリアは既知の風土病であり、本記事は定例の罹患率報告であって異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: マラリアはパプア地域で既知の風土病であり、国の保健当局が2027年対策を議論する定例の疫学報告記事。新規性・異常性は低く、ヒト-ヒト感染もないためDISMISS相当と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Prevent TB Transmission, Unmul Equips Samarinda Health Cadres with the CARE-TB Program.
article.articleSummary: TB control in Samarinda, Indonesia advances through Universitas Mulawarman’s CARE-TB program, targeting improved Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) adherence among families of TB patients. Part of the Community-Based Empowerment Scheme under the 2026 PKM BIMA program and funded by the Directorate General of Research and Development, Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology, CARE-TB is led by Dr. Vina Maulidya with a multidisciplinary team and involves 15 health cadres in Samarinda, in partnership with Yayasan Penabulu Samarinda. The initiative aims to raise cadres’ knowledge to at least 80%, increase family understanding to 75%, and achieve 70% TPT adherence among targeted households. Challenges include insufficient TPT-specific training (about 80% of cadres) and reliance on oral information without standardized educational media (about 73%), compounded by TB stigma. The program seeks to empower cadres to educate and support families affected by TB.

triage.headline_ja: 結核感染予防のため、ムラワルマン大学がサマリンダの保健カードルにCARE-TBプログラムを提供
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムの教育活動に関する記事であり、異常な公衆衛生事象や新規アウトブレイクの報告ではないため。
triage.notes: 地域情報にIndonesiaが含まれるが、記事内容は既存の結核予防教育プログラムの紹介であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事象の報告ではないため、シグナルとしては扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: Persistent cough? Watch out for this disease.
article.articleSummary: Jakarta, Indonesia – A persistent cough requires evaluation for several conditions. Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) is a major concern when cough lasts two weeks or more, often with sputum, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and fatigue; it is airborne. Other causes include chronic bronchitis from long-term smoking or pollution, with a recurrent productive cough and chest discomfort; asthma, featuring recurrent cough, especially at night or after exercise, with wheeze; pneumonia, an infection causing productive cough, fever, chest pain, and shortness of breath; and GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease), where reflux irritates the throat and triggers coughing after meals or when lying down, sometimes with heartburn. Seek care if cough exceeds two weeks or is accompanied by fever, night sweats, weight loss, chest pain, blood in sputum, or breathing difficulty. Diagnostic steps may include physical exam, sputum tests, and chest X-ray.

triage.headline_ja: 咳が長引く？この病気に注意
triage.triage_reason: 特定のアウトブレイクではなく、持続する咳の鑑別診断に関する一般的な健康啓発記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Subang Health Office Finds 284 New HIV Cases, 52 Patients Have Died.
article.articleSummary: Subang District Health Office reports a sharp rise in HIV/AIDS in 2026, with 284 new HIV cases recorded through September 2026 and 52 deaths. SIHA data show most fatalities occur at advanced HIV disease, with deaths mainly from opportunistic infections rather than the virus itself, notably tuberculosis, toxoplasmosis, and pneumonia, indicating severe immune compromise. Of the 284 new cases, 89 (about one-third) are men who have sex with men (MSM). Transmission is dominated by risky sexual contact and needle-sharing. The outbreak extends beyond urban areas and now spans multiple locations within Subang Regency. Health officials urge heightened vigilance and advise avoiding unsafe sex, high-risk same-sex activity, and injecting drug use to interrupt transmission. The report covers January–September 2026, highlighting ongoing outbreak management and prevention efforts.

triage.headline_ja: スバン県保健局、新規HIV感染284例を確認、52人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: HIV/AIDSは既知の地域流行性疾患であり、国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態や渡航制限等のリスクはなく、IHR基準・WPRO基準いずれも該当性が低い。
triage.notes: 地域限定的なHIV/AIDS流行の報告であり、国際的な公衆衛生緊急事態には該当しない。国内保健当局による既存の対応枠組み内での管理が可能と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Cirebon City Government Intensifies TB Contact Tracing to Households.
article.articleSummary: TB in Cirebon City, West Java, Indonesia, prompts intensified contact tracing targeting households and close contacts to curb transmission and prevent new cases. Deputy Mayor Siti Farida Rosmawati says management must begin with early case finding, ensuring patients receive treatment and support to completion. Household members and nearby residents should undergo health screenings to detect TB exposure quickly. Multi-sectoral involvement is emphasized to reach residents with contact histories who have not yet screened. The program reports a TB case-finding rate of 191% in Cirebon, influenced by patients from outside the city using local facilities. The Kelurahan Siaga TB (TB Alert Villages) now covers all 22 kelurahan, underpinning community prevention and case finding. TB screening is integrated with the Free Health Check program across 99 service points. The initiative also provides Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) for eligible groups, highlighting treatment completion and ongoing family and community support.

triage.headline_ja: チルボン市政府、結核の濃厚接触者追跡を家庭にまで強化
triage.triage_reason: 結核は地域の風土病であり、通常の対策プログラムの一環としての報道であるため、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 結核対策の通常業務（コンタクトトレーシング、スクリーニング強化）に関する地域行政の取り組み報告であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: US Stands To Lose Measles Elimination Status As Multiple States Face The Worst Outbreaks In Nearly Three Decades - Health Policy Watch
article.articleSummary: Measles elimination in the United States faces collapse as PAHO is expected to revoke the country's elimination status after more than two decades of low endemic transmission. Through 2026, CDC reports over 5,200 measles cases in the United States, with six deaths cited by CDC and two additional fatalities in New York and Wisconsin, totaling eight. Outbreaks across Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, Utah and other states have prompted emergency declarations and urgent vaccination appeals. For the first time in decades, outbreaks are primarily locally transmitted rather than imported, with Utah's outbreak persisting for more than a year. PAHO will base its decision on genetic sequencing to determine whether a single viral genotype is driving nationwide transmission. The 2025–2026 wave follows earlier imported cases; Mexico and several other countries may also lose elimination status, reflecting a global burden concentrated in Bangladesh, Indonesia, Guatemala, India, Yemen, Pakistan and Angola.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、複数州で過去30年近くで最悪規模の麻疹アウトブレイクに直面し、麻疹排除認定を失う可能性
triage.triage_reason: 米国内で8例の死亡と5,200例超の麻疹症例が報告され、PAHOによる排除認定取り消しの可能性があるなど、公衆衛生上深刻かつ異常な事態であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべき案件。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は米国での麻疹アウトブレイクとPAHOによる排除認定取り消しの可能性。インドネシア・インド等は世界的な麻疹負担の文脈で言及されているのみで、記事の主題ではないため対象国として含めない。米国・メキシコは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: Indonesia Free TB Screening Finds 700,000 Cases, but Treatment Success Misses Targets
article.articleSummary: Indonesia's free health checkups identified more than 700,000 tuberculosis cases this year, with 90% of flagged patients starting treatment. Yet TB control remains short of targets: 80% treatment success for drug-sensitive TB (target 90%), and 58% for drug-resistant TB (target 80%). SITB data show 84% treatment starts against a 95% target. The 700,000 cases estimate equals about 64% of an annual 1.09 million TB burden, implying many cases remain unfound. Since April 2026, SATUSEHAT IndonesiaKu checkups data exchange with SITB enables automatic recognition of TB patients and fast-tracks high-risk suspects for testing; AI-assisted X-ray screening has examined ~200,000 people, flagging about 4,000 suspected TB among 38,000 scans. Drug-resistant TB: 26% fail to complete therapy; six-month all-oral BPaLM regimens yield 86–89% success versus ~52% for older regimens. To curb transmission, renovations are planned for 2,000 homes in 2026 and 10,000 in 2027 for low-income households.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアの無料結核検診で70万件の症例を発見、治療成功率は目標未達
triage.triage_reason: 既知の慢性疾患である結核の国内対策進捗に関する定例報告であり、新規性・急性の公衆衛生上の脅威はなく、国際的拡大リスクも認められない。
triage.notes: 結核対策プログラムの進捗報告であり、国家の公衆衛生政策・保健システム運営に関する情報。緊急シグナルではなく通常の保健統計報告。

article.articleHeadline: East Kalimantan Health Office reminds of the leptospirosis risk as the rainy season begins.
article.articleSummary: East Kalimantan health authorities warn of heightened leptospirosis risk as the rainy season begins in Samarinda. Leptospirosis, caused by Leptospira bacteria, spreads via floodwater and damp environments contaminated with urine from rats, dogs, and livestock. Transmission occurs through skin or mucous membranes contacting contaminated water or soil, or by drinking contaminated water. Early symptoms include sudden fever, calf-muscle pain, and severe headaches; delayed treatment can lead to kidney and liver damage, lung involvement, and meningitis, with severe Weil’s disease causing kidney failure, jaundice, and bleeding. Preventive guidance from the Health Office and Gerakan Masyarakat Hidup Sehat emphasizes four steps: avoid direct contact with contaminated standing water and always wear boots; use gloves when cleaning surroundings; control rodent nests and maintain home sanitation; boil drinking water and keep food hygienically covered. Seek care at a puskesmas if high fever after contact with floodwater.

triage.headline_ja: 東カリマンタン保健局、雨季到来に伴うレプトスピラ症リスクについて注意喚起
triage.triage_reason: 具体的な症例発生報告ではなく、雨季到来に伴う一般的な予防啓発記事であり、異常性・緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は具体的な感染者数や症例データを含まず、季節的な注意喚起（予防啓発）であるため、シグナルとしての優先度は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Thailand Reports 61 Suspected Diphtheria Cases and Eight Deaths as Deadly Southern Cluster Raises Alarm
article.articleSummary: Thailand reports 61 suspected diphtheria cases and eight deaths from January 1 to November 9, 2026, with a case fatality rate of about 13.1%. No nationwide outbreak is evident, but localized transmission is evident in the south. The three southern border provinces and four Songkhla districts account for 21 suspected cases and five deaths (34.4% of infections; 62.5% of fatalities). Narathiwat Province has the highest southern burden with ten suspected cases. Eight toxin-confirmed infections have been identified nationwide, including four deaths; five confirmed infections and three deaths occur in the southern focus. Patients range from 8 months to 82 years, median age 18, with children under four most affected due to immunization gaps. Diphtheria symptoms include sore throat, fever, weakness, swollen neck glands and a gray membrane; toxin can cause myocarditis, paralysis, respiratory failure. Public health response emphasizes rapid detection, contact tracing, vaccination campaigns, antitoxin readiness, and prompt treatment when strongly suspected.

triage.headline_ja: タイで61例のジフテリア疑い例と8人の死亡、南部で致死的クラスター発生し警戒強まる
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準を2つ以上満たし（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な集積発生）、南部国境県での致死率13.1%の死亡例集積とワクチンギャップによる感受性人口の存在が確認されるためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 南部国境3県とソンクラ県4地区に感染が集中。毒素確認例8例中4例死亡。4歳未満児の罹患が多くワクチン接種率低下が示唆される。国境地域での発生のため近隣国（マレーシア等、対象国リスト外）への波及リスクにも留意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: China Admits Flu Surge Involving Three Strains but Questions Remain Over Possible Fourth Reassortant Strain
article.articleSummary: China reports rising influenza activity with three circulating strains: A(H3N2), A(H1N1), and influenza B. Northern provinces show moderate activity, while southern regions report higher transmission; school-aged children 5–14 have higher positivity. For Nov 2–8, influenza had the highest positivity among respiratory pathogens in sentinel hospitals, with rhinoviruses second. Hospitalizations are increasing in Liaoning, Guangxi, Jiangxi, and Hubei, notably in the first three provinces. Reports, via Thailand Medical News, raise questions about a possible fourth reassortant virus combining avian H9N2 and swine-origin H1N2v; official surveillance omits such a strain, prompting concerns about concealment by some local virologists and doctors. China CDC stresses that respiratory activity typically peaks November–March and urges prompt vaccination for children, older adults, individuals with chronic illnesses, and workers in schools, childcare, nursing homes, and hospitals. Expanded laboratory surveillance and transparent reporting are urged until genetic confirmation clarifies whether a fourth strain exists.

article.articleHeadline: Nakhon Ratchasima fears a fever that causes deafness! 76 ill, 9 dead. Warns that eating raw pork poses a life-threatening risk.
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus suis infection causing fever with potential permanent deafness remains active in Nakhon Ratchasima Province, Thailand, within Health Region 9. From January 1 to November 11, 2026, Nakhon Ratchasima reported 76 cases and 9 deaths (incidence 2.75 per 100,000; case fatality rate 11.84%; mortality 0.35 per 100,000). Older adults, especially those aged 70+, are most affected. Transmission is linked to eating raw or undercooked pork and exposure to pork blood; symptoms include fever, chills, myalgia, dyspnea, severe headache, vomiting, and neck stiffness, with potential progression to meningitis, bacteremia, deafness, endocarditis, or death. Authorities installed warning signs in markets (Nong Phai Lom, Ya Mo, Pratu Chai Narong, Suranaree, Hua Rot Fai markets) and advised thorough cooking and strict separation of raw vs cooked meat and utensils. NR districts with higher case numbers include Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Phimai, Khamsa Kaeng, and Dan Khun Thot. Other Region 9 provinces reporting cases: Chaiyaphum 27/3, Buriram 25/1, Surin 15/1.

article.articleHeadline: Iloilo City Ramps Up Anti-Dengue Efforts Amid Rising Cases and Fatalities
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Iloilo City, Philippines, rose to 785 cases and eight deaths from January through October 2026, a 37.7% increase versus the same period last year and breaching alert and epidemic thresholds. Twenty-eight barangays report case clusters (three infections within four weeks); four villages are hotspots due to confirmed fatalities, with October deaths in Barangays Boulevard (Molo), San Isidro (Jaro), and Baldoza (La Paz), following earlier fatalities in February and August. The City Health Office is intensifying the Department of Health's 4S strategy, emphasizing search and destroy of mosquito breeding sites and early medical consultation at nine district health centers, alongside self-protection measures and fogging when warranted. Regular misting occurs in schools and public facilities, while the sanitation division deploys teams to bolster intensified cleanup; dengue task forces and health emergency teams have been active since September to track suspected infections and promote preventive practices.

article.articleHeadline: Novel Real-Time PCR Detects Rabies in Canine Muzzle and Nasal Samples
article.articleSummary: Novel real-time RT-qPCR detects rabies virus in non-brain post-mortem canine tissues, enabling diagnosis when brain tissue is inaccessible. A collaboration including the Philippines Research Institute for Tropical Medicine, Oita University, Kitasato University, the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, and Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology targeted the nucleoprotein gene of the Southeast Asia 4 clade. Compared with the direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) test, the assay showed complete positive agreement across brain, muzzle follicle-sinus complex, and nasal planum samples from dogs suspected of infection. Peripheral tissues thus harbor detectable viral material during terminal disease, supporting decentralized surveillance without invasive cranial procedures. Rabies is a lethal zoonosis; globally about 59,000 deaths annually, with dogs accounting for up to 99% of human cases. In the Philippines, endemic transmission rose from 200–300 cases around 2020 to over 350 in 2022–2023; vaccination coverage was 53.3% in 2018.

article.articleHeadline: Female genital schistosomiasis: a prevalence of nearly 25%...
article.articleSummary: Female genital schistosomiasis prevalence is about 25% in the Richard-Toll and Podor health districts in Senegal’s Saint-Louis region, based on a study in Saint-Louis. Governor Al Hassan Sall calls the finding very concerning and urges strong community mobilization. The study, led by the National Program for Neglected Tropical Diseases and Dr Ndèye Mbacké Kane, involves Université Gaston Berger and Université Cheikh Anta Diop, with work in Mali, Ghana, Nigeria and Madagascar. Genital schistosomiasis, caused by Schistosoma parasites, damages genital tissues via eggs, causing lesions, pain and possible fertility issues. Risk is highest for women and girls with contact with contaminated freshwater during domestic, agricultural or recreational activities (laundry, dishes, rice fields, bathing) in the Senegal River delta and valley. Recommendations: integrate screening into routine health services, sustain mass treatment, and mobilize communities. Malaria context: 2025 saw 2,734 cases and two deaths in Saint-Louis; none in early 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Côte d'Ivoire-AIP/ Prof. Jérémie Zoueu advocates spectral imaging to improve malaria diagnosis.
article.articleSummary: Malaria diagnosis could be revolutionized by spectral imaging, according to Prof. Jérémie Zoueu, coordinator of the African Network for Spectral Imaging (AFSIN) in Songon, Ivory Coast. At the 15th AFSIN workshop closing Oct 29, 2026 at the Swiss Center for Scientific Research (CSRS) in Adiopodoumé, Zoueu described an optical device that uses light interactions with cells to distinguish healthy from malaria-infected cells in minutes, bypassing traditional thick smear and blood smear methods that take hours. The CSRS-developed system is already operational there and is undergoing miniaturization to yield a compact, user-friendly instrument operable by laboratory technicians with a single command, enabling deployment in clinics and local health centers. The event gathered researchers from Ivory Coast, Sweden, Germany, Ghana, Burkina Faso, Mali, Togo, Cameroon, and Kenya, to advance light-based life-science technologies.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases exceed 11,000 as Africa CDC warns of challenges
article.articleSummary: Six months into the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, Africa CDC reports 11,145 confirmed cases and 5,437 deaths (fatality 48.8%), with 3,058 recoveries. The Democratic Republic of the Congo remains the epicentre, grappling with security concerns, surveillance gaps, rising community transmission, and infections among health workers that hamper containment. Only about 11% of new cases are linked to known contacts, far below the 95% target, reflecting weak contact listing and tracing amid insecurity. Kenya reports its first imported case on Oct 6, nine confirmed cases and two deaths; the last patient has been discharged and 11 contacts completed 21-day monitoring. Nigeria notes 62 contacts identified, 59 completed monitoring, three under observation. Ten other nations—South Sudan, Rwanda, Zambia, Central African Republic, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Somalia—are designated high-risk. Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on May 18; WHO declared a PHEIC on May 17.

article.articleHeadline: Free measles and rubella vaccination continues in Katha - Global New Light Of Myanmar
article.articleSummary: Measles and rubella vaccination campaign in Katha District, Myanmar, offering free supplementary vaccines for infants and children aged nine months to five years at City Hall from 8 am. Dr Phyu Pya Min, Deputy Director of the District Public Health Department, supervised; health staff administered vaccines. Oversight by Katha District Management Administration Committee Chairman U Htin Kyaw and Katha Township Committee Chairman U Than Tun with members; a health official provided parents with information on vaccine-preventable diseases and immunization benefits. The drive ran 9–13 November, and by 13 November a total of 17,800 children had received vaccines, per the Katha District Public Health Department.
